the positive effect of warming on growth of Quercous myrsinaefolium saplings was attenuated by a reduction in NAR caused by high daily mean air temperatures exceeding 30 ° C, but the negative effect was compensated by an increase in NAR caused mainly by CO 2 enrichment, resulting in an almost twofold increase in the annual biomass production by the combined effects of warming and CO 2 elevation.
